As Donald Trump continued his attacks on Iran earlier this month, a deal that could radically reshape security in the Middle East was quietly being done in Saudi Arabia.

On 7 August, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey signed the Mecca Joint Defence agreement, a Nato-style mutual defence pact that states an attack on any one of the group will be considered an attack on all.

The timing is significant. All three countries have been the target of Iranian retaliatory attacks across the Middle East since US-Israeli strikes killed supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in February.

Turkey boasts the second largest army in Nato (second only to the US), while Saudi Arabia is the second-most oil rich nation on the planet. Pakistan is a nuclear power that has also acted as a broker between the US and Iran throughout the ongoing conflict.

But although Trump praised the agreement on Sunday as an example of the countries “finally being able to defend themselves in a more meaningful way”, experts say the agreement marks a major shift in the global world order – away from the US.

open image in gallery From left, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif pose after signing a trilateral defense agreement in Mecca, Saudi Arabia, 7 August 2026. ( AP )

Deal is ‘a response to US and Israeli military action’

Hugh Lovatt, a senior policy fellow at the EU’s European Council on Foreign Relations, says that the realignment can be seen as “a response to the conflict and a way for some of these actors to try and secure themselves”.

“It is also unavoidable as a response to Israel’s increasing regional aggressiveness.”

Mr Lovatt says that Israeli attacks on Doha in Qatar last year during the country’s war in Gaza “shook the region” and that Turkish and Gulf officials had told him they feared they would be next.

Israel has recently launched strikes in several countries including Syria, Lebanon, Iran, Yemen and Qatar, according to Acled data analysed by Al Jazeera, as well as continuing attacks in Gaza and the occupied West Bank.

Tel Aviv’s “hegemonic ambitions” are increasing threat perceptions on the ground, he adds. Trump has also shown no hesitation in threatening to attack his allies, saying he would “bomb the s**t” out of Oman on Monday.

open image in gallery New Hamas leader Khalil al Hayya was the intended target of an Israeli attack on Doha ( AFP/Getty )

Trump is ‘unreliable’

“The US remains indispensable for the region, but it is also unpredictable and unreliable,” says Galip Dalay, a senior research fellow for the Middle East and North Africa at Chatham House.

Reflecting on the Trump-brokered Abraham Accords signed in 2020 to normalise relations between Arab states and Israel, he explains that the “central weakness of the US vision is that it did not have a place for the Palestinian question”.

“It did not have a vision for non-Arab state actors. This agreement signals a post-Abrahamic regional reordering and represents the failure of the Abrahamic vision but it is still not inherently anti-Israel.”

All three countries have expressed a reluctance to normalise relations with Tel Aviv, with both Saudi Arabia and Pakistan effectively banning Israeli citizens from entering the country.

open image in gallery Trump and Middle East leaders at the White House after the signing of the Abraham Accords ( AFP/Getty )

But despite this, Lovatt believes that the three countries are seeking to find common ground on security issues rather than outright rejecting the US.

Signatories to the Abraham Accords, including the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Morocco and Sudan, have faced backlash in the Arab world for normalising relations with Israel.

While Iran’s proxy network, including Hezbollah in Lebanon, the Houthis in Yemen and Hamas in Palestine, is transparently the most hostile towards the west, experts say the Mecca group represents a middle ground: seeking partnership with Washington but showing suspicion towards Israeli ambitions in the Middle East.

“I would call it a counter-Abraham Accords axis,” Lovatt says, noting that the group is not strictly religious in nature despite its framing as a “Muslim Nato”.

Sharing the burden

However, the US will be eager to position the announcement as an example of countries sharing the burden of defence with less dependence on Washington – in keeping with Trump’s demands.

“You can see quite clearly that Turkey and Saudi Arabia are rising middle powers and now these aspiring regional powers are trying to influence the geopolitical order in the Middle East to their advantage,” says Lovatt.

“But from a rational US strategic viewpoint, this is not a threat to US regional ambitions. If they had partnered with Russia or China, it would be different.

open image in gallery Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan is received by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, ahead of the expected signing of a defence deal between Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey, in Mecca, Saudi Arabia, 7 August 2026. ( Reuters )

“This is an intra-regional alignment and all three countries have very close relations to the US. They are it’s partners and allies so the US is unlikely to see this as a threat.

“You could even make the argument that this plays to US ambitions to encourage regional partners to do more to defend themselves and ensure their own security and defence in terms of burden-sharing”.

However, the close relationship between the US and Israel could affect this thinking if Israel – which hopes to become a Middle Eastern “superpower” itself according to Netanyahu – sees the alliance as a threat to its own ambitions.

It has already made no secret of its hostility towards Turkey, with Netanyahu accusing Ankara of having “aggressive aspirations”. Saudi Arabia could be considered a positive actor in relation to Israel, but there is no guarantee of its future position, he says.

open image in gallery ( Reuters )

What does the agreement mean in practice?

Although the Houthis have continued to attack Saudi targets in the aftermath of the signing, the pact is yet to be truly tested. After all, Nato’s Article 5 has only ever been triggered once, after the 9/11 attacks in 2001.

Erdogan has directly likened it to the Nato rule and said that the Mecca agreement “applies in a similar way”. He has also said: “This is not limited solely to the Kingdom of Saudis, Turkey, and Pakistan. Other countries may also join us. Egypt too, if it wishes, can join the agreement with these three countries. The doors are open to Egypt.”

Lovatt believes that the alliance could prove most effective in the sphere of diplomacy.

“Nato is more than just some members working together,” he says.

“This alignment has the most value and could be the most impactful in the diplomatic sphere, where these countries act together in pursuit of a common regional vision.”

President Trump has claimed that those opposing his White House ballroom project are “disloyal” to the United States.​

The ballroom is at the center of a court battle over whether work on the project can continue to go ahead, with questions also raised over plans to build a military complex beneath the site.

Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office on Monday, Trump dismissed criticism of the costly endeavour, which is being built on the former site of the East Wing of the White House.

“The people that are opposing the ballroom are people that, in my opinion, are very disloyal to our country,” he said. “And I think we’re doing well.

“We’re way ahead of schedule,” he continued. “We’re under budget. It’s going to be the most beautiful ballroom of its kind.”

open image in gallery President Trump shared an AI-generated video of himself showing former President George Washington around the ballroom ( @realDonaldTrump/Truth Social )

Trump has long boasted about the ballroom project, even sharing a surreal A.I.-generated video of himself showing former President George Washington around the complex.

“Thank you, George, for some of your brilliant ideas on this great Military Complex/Ballroom,” Trump captioned the video on Sunday.

Speaking to reporters on Monday, Trump suggested that the military had approached him about the project.​

“When I said that I was going to build a ballroom, the military asked if they could see me,” he said.

“And, they say: ‘Sir, we have an opportunity to go down deep into the ground and build a military facility to go with the White House and to go with all of Washington D.C.’ - which would be so valuable.”

open image in gallery Trump told reporters that the military approached him about building a facility under the ballroom ( Reuters )

“And, all of those things added up, and it became much more than just a ballroom,” he said, noting that officials also floated adding a drone port to the facility.

An appeals court has ordered construction of the ballroom to be halted by August 21 unless Congress green-lights the project. The decision still allows Trump to continue building the underground military facility.

On Friday, his administration officials asked the Supreme Court to allow the ballroom aspect of the project to go ahead.​

“Today, the Project is 65% complete in its entirety, and moving quickly toward total completion,” U.S. Solicitor General D. John Sauer wrote in his filing.

Speaking on Monday, Trump also defended his wider efforts to beautify the White House, claiming that it had been “let go” before he became president.

“We’re fixing the White House that hasn’t been taken care of,” he said. “The White House was let go. The exteriors were falling apart, the columns were falling apart. The whole place was a mess.”

The smell of incense, burning palo santo and dried sage practically emanates through my laptop screen. I am trawling through Etsy, the online marketplace known for handmade kitsch ornaments and unofficial Taylor Swift merch — to find a witch.

Not just any witch: I am looking for one who can provide me with a spell to mend my broken heart after a two-year relationship ... and tell me how to navigate the cesspit that is modern dating.

Self-styled Etsy witches — people who offer witchcraft services online — are selling spells, manifestations and tarot readings on Etsy and TikTok, promising everything from good weather on your wedding day to a new job or even a small fortune.

On my journey to find one, I scroll past oddly specific spell offerings like: “Get him to text you back,” "Make him obsessed" and “Get your ex back” (this one does catch my eye, but I resist). Then I hit the jackpot: a witch with 4,000+ sales, a 4.9-star rating, and a tagline that reads, “Tell me nothing and I’ll tell you everything.”

Just take my money already.

open image in gallery Heartbreak has become big business for online witches. Some of them offer services to ‘enter the mind’ of your former lover to find out what they’re thinking; others will promise to banish them from your life or even make them regret dumping you ( Oscilloscope Laboratories )

For the humble sum of $4.08, I select the spell and “detailed reading” option before dropping my somewhat desperate yet burning question: When will I find love again? As I hit purchase, I glance at the performative healing crystals gathering dust on my desk (they were a gift, OK?), and decide now is as good a time as any to start believing in them.

Heartbreak has become big business for online witches. Some of them offer services to “enter the mind” of your former lover to find out what they’re thinking; others will promise to banish them from your life or even make them regret dumping you. These services have become so popular that Etsy banned the sale of spells, enchantments, and any supernatural service in 2015. However, they are still being sold on the platform under “entertainment services” (The Independent has contacted Etsy for comment).

Etsy witches are being enlisted as armchair relationship gurus because modern dating is truly in the gutter right now. In a recent article published in The Atlantic titled “The Great Romance Slump,” a journalist argues that there is a “bounty of possibility” in the modern dating world – you can meet people on apps, at singles events and in socially vibrant cities – but fewer people, especially the young, are actually finding love, due to a product of broader trends that include souring gender relations, the unevenness of social progress and technology that can both connect and isolate us.

The statistics are staggering. The proportion of 25- to 34-year-olds in marriages or cohabiting partnerships dropped steeply from 1980 to 2022 — by almost 10 percent for college graduates and more than 20 percent for people without a degree, according to an analysis by the Financial Times.

Modern dating has made even basic communication feel fraught. Even if you meet someone organically, there's no guarantee you'll escape ghosting — the now-familiar practice of disappearing without explanation. Getting a simple text back can feel like an achievement in itself. Things have become so bleak that women are even being ghosted by their long-term partners, according to a recent Vogue article.

open image in gallery Etsy has dozens of options to choose from when it comes to witchcraft, from love spells to manifestations ( Etsy )

With so much uncertainty around dating, can my Etsy witch give me a glimmer of hope? A few hours after I hit purchase, her response arrives in my inbox. At first glance, I wonder whether it has been crafted by ChatGPT because her 3,200-word reading (!) is split up by subheadings that have emojis next to them, but the further I read, I’m blown away by how quickly my witch understands my current predicament.

She tells me that I am not closed to love, but “no longer want a connection that begins beautifully and then leaves you questioning their emotional availability.” Granted, this could apply to almost anyone who is newly single, but what my witch said next changed my outlook on dating forever…

The most startling insight came when she identified my “biggest blind spot”: that I see potential in a relationship before the other person proves to me there is any. I couldn’t have agreed more; I admit I have a tendency to get carried away and assume things about an imaginary future before really getting to know someone.

open image in gallery For centuries, people have turned to the occult for cosmic intervention during difficult times ( Disney )

“You can sense the softer side of someone, understand why they are guarded, and imagine the relationship they could create if they healed or became more emotionally available,” my witch tells me. “This can make you loyal to a future version of the person.”

I send this paragraph to my equally impressed friend. Then I wonder whether my Etsy witch ever considered a career as a licensed therapist. It might be too soon to say, but maybe she’s healed me?

“You need to ask who they are now. Are they communicating now? Are they consistent now? Are they ready to participate now?” she writes to me. “Growth is possible, but you should not be required to remain uncertain while someone slowly decides whether they want to become capable of love.” I want to get that last sentence tattooed on my arm.

She also tells me that my strongest romantic window will appear within approximately four to eight months, so there is hope yet. Apparently, my future beau will “feel calmer, grounded, emotionally observant, and more consistent than someone connected to your past.” Ideal.

open image in gallery Love spells have been traced all the way back to 2,200 BCE, but today, you can find someone online to summon your former lover back to you ( Oscilloscope Laboratories )

For centuries, people have turned to the occult for cosmic intervention during difficult times (love spells have been traced all the way back to 2,200 BCE). Today, though, it is no longer taboo to hire a witch for some spellwork. Although it's unclear which tradition my Etsy witch follows, modern witchcraft encompasses a wide range of practices. Some identify with Wicca, a modern, Earth-focused pagan religion, while others describe themselves as eclectic witches, drawing from different spiritual traditions; green witches, who work with elements of nature; or solitary witches, who practise alone.

For most clients, however, the finer points of a witch’s practice are beside the point. They’re not shopping for a particular tradition — they’re looking for reassurance, guidance, or simply the feeling that something ethereal is on their side.

And in my case, my witch has provided me with some hope when I definitely needed it. Alongside my reading, we also cast a spell for abundance in my future. I’m still waiting for that one to kick in, but I’m expecting good things.

For $4.08, this was money well spent, even if the legitimacy of my witch is a little hazy. In a dating culture where people treat each other as increasingly disposable, turning to a stranger on the internet for answers may feel absurd, but it turned out to be the reality check I needed. I do feel a little lighter.

Whoever it is behind the screen — a genuine witch, an exceptionally perceptive stranger or someone armed with ChatGPT — she’s found a satisfied customer in me. In my Etsy DMs, I thank her for her spell and reading, and ask if we can make this a regular thing. Call it a quarterly check-in. “I would be so grateful,” she replies. “With love and light.”

Three more earthquakes have hit Spain's southern Granada province, causing some damage to buildings and forcing the closure of some museums and sports facilities, including the medieval Alhambra complex, where tourist access was restricted.

The earthquakes on Tuesday each had magnitudes above 4, the country's National Geographic Institute (IGN) said.

At least three people were lightly injured, Andalusia's regional top emergency official Antonio Sanz told reporters, adding that one of them, a minor, was taken to hospital.

The tremors followed Saturday's 5.0-magnitude earthquake in the historic city of Granada, which damaged houses and cars and forced the temporary closure of the medieval palace-fortress of the Alhambra, one of Spain's main tourist sites that was visited by 2.7 million people last year.

Following Saturday’s earthquake, Mr Sanz said there was no damage to the Alhambra palace.

"There is no serious structural damage, no serious material damage and there are no casualties," he said, adding that the Alhambra had "not been affected in any way".

A damaged wall is cordoned off in the aftermath of an earthquake ( Reuters )

This time, authorities at the Alhambra interrupted tourist access to parts of the sprawling complex on a hill above the city, which is a monument of Islamic architecture in Spain.

The provincial authority of Granada said in a statement it was closing administrative buildings, museums and sporting facilities but kept primary health centres open for now.

Granada's metro system said on social media platform X it was reducing the speed of its trains to 30 kph (19 mph) as a precautionary measure, and local media showed several hotels being evacuated.

Some buildings, mostly residential, suffered damage in the tremors, with large cracks showing in the walls, parts of some facades dislodged and bricks strewn across pavements.

The largest of Tuesday's quakes, with a magnitude of 4.7, occurred at 10:37 a.m. (0837 GMT) and had its surface-level epicentre in the town of Gojar, 10 km (6 miles) south of Granada city, the IGN said. Surface-level quakes are felt more intensely and are more likely to cause localised damage to buildings than a deeper tremor of similar strength.

The Gojar earthquake was quickly followed by slightly lighter tremors in two nearby towns on Granada's southern outskirts.

The owner of Poundland is reportedly looking to sell the discount high street store just a year after it took over.

The bargain prices shop saw 200 of its stores close after Gordon Brothers purchased it last year but still employs around 12,000 people across the UK.

However, despite claims of an upturn in performance since the buyout, Sky News reports that Gordon Brothers is in talks over a potential auction process sale, with advisers to oversee the deal set to be appointed in the coming days.

There are approximately 600 stores remaining in the UK after those initial closures, which had to be approved by a High Court judge through a restructuring plan.

In its most recently filed accounts, Poundland made a £79m pre-tax loss in the year to September 2024, but earlier this year managing director Barry Williams said there had been “significant progress” within the company, while still noting there was “much to do” in the turnaround efforts.

“Our focus on our costs has, without doubt, given us a platform for future growth, but no sustainable turnaround can be based on cost management alone,” he said in January.

“That's why our focus in 2026 will be on delivering the kind of ranges and price simplicity our customers want right across the store - in clothing, homewares as well as our core grocery aisles.”

A spokesperson for Poundland declined to respond to Sky on the sale reports, but said: “We've made very significant progress over the past year with a recovery plan that's created simpler, better value for customers centred around thousands of items back at our iconic £1 price point.”

Gordon Brothers, which is based in Boston in the United States, has not stated any reason for the potential sale. But the firm owns a large selection of assets and businesses, many of which are listed for sale, lease, auction or investment – all of which are part of the wider group’s typical model of buying and restructuring or selling on assets.

In the UK, that includes a wood-fired pizza restaurant in London, the recently collapsed motorcycle retailer Superbike Factory and a clothing distributor and online retailer referred to only as “Project Beluga”.

The Independent has contacted Gordon Brothers for comment.

News.title: Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal get Alvarez update, Chelsea set new Enzo price, Liverpool reach deal for PSG winger
News.content:
Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone has confirmed that he will bench star striker and Arsenal target Julian Alvarez for their LaLiga opener on Wednesday as he remains locked in a transfer dispute over his future. Alvarez is pushing to join Barcelona this summer, with Atletico CEO Miguel Angel Gil Marin saying the club would not even accept €200m for the former Manchester City forward. Arsenal are hoping to land a marquee attacking signing this summer ahead of their Premier League title defence.

Manchester City face a price hike if they are to sign Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea. City are still interested in signing Fernandez despite missing Chelsea’s Friday deadline for offers, but now face paying much more than the £120m the Blues were demanding last week. Chelsea want the midfielder’s future to be resolved before their opening game of the season this weekend. City, meanwhile, are to sign 18-year-old midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi for £85m after selling Ballon d’Or winner Rodri to Barcelona in a deal worth up to £65m.

Elsewhere, Manchester United are set to reject an audacious approach from Galatasaray for their captain Bruno Fernandes. The Turkish club are determined to sign a star this summer and are lining up a comprehensive financial package that would have doubled the 31-year-old midfielder’s salary, but United’s stance is that Fernandes is not for sale. Fernandes has entered the final 12 months of his contract at Old Trafford, but there is an option to extend for another year, and United are also set to open discussions on a new deal.

Liverpool have agreed terms with Paris Saint-Germain forward Ibrahim Mbaye and also want to sign Bradely Barcola, according to reports in France. Both Mbaye, 18, and France international Barcola were left out of PSG’s squad for the French Super Cup on Sunday. The European champions were set to demand £145m for Barcola, who is also wanted by Arsenal, but Liverpool are prepared to play the long-game as they bid to negotiate a price.

A manhunt is underway in Philadelphia after a suspect in a Chucky-style mask threatened and chased multiple people, asking one woman if she was “ready to die”, according to police.

Footage shows a masked man in dark clothing chasing a woman jogging near City Hall in the Center City neighborhood at around 5:30a.m. on Wednesday, 12 August.

He is accused of harassing at least six people over a period of nearly 20 minutes, wearing a “distinctive Chucky doll Halloween-style face mask,” Philadelphia Police Captain Jason Smith said in a press briefing Monday.

The suspect faces charges of harassment, terroristic threats, simple assault, reckless endangerment and intimidation, he added, per ABC News.

open image in gallery The masked man was spotted on several security cameras ( Philadelphia Police Department )

While chasing the jogger, the masked man was “holding his cellphone in front of her, at which point he asked her, 'Are you ready to die?'”, Smith said.

“The female is screaming for help this entire time… The male abruptly stops and heads northbound on 15th Street, at which point he gets on the escalators at Suburban Station,” Smith explained, per 6abc Action News.

As of Monday, Smith said only the jogger had come forward to police, although there were believed to be at least half a dozen people the suspect had been “attempting to scare or antagonize”, he said according to ABC News.

open image in gallery Philadelphia cops released multiple images and footage in connection with the case ( Philadelphia Police Department )

A witness described the bizarre encounter, telling reporters it was “like some twisted game”.

Luanda Marinho told CBS News: “He starts asking, ‘Do you guys want to race me? I bet I am faster than you. Want to race me?’ He asked a few times, but none of us acknowledged him. Very weird.

”We're scared, so now we're thinking about changing our routes or changing our schedules, which shouldn't be an issue,” she added. “It was just weird, like some twisted game."

Another woman recalled fighting off the suspect by kicking him in the chest, after trying to warn the jogger that there was someone behind her.

open image in gallery The man was spotted chasing a jogger on a security camera ( Fox29/The Philadelphia Police Department )

Speaking to 6abc, Jameka, who gave only her first name, said the jogger was wearing headphones when she was approached.

”I started to wave at her from across the intersection and say, 'Hey there's someone behind you, look behind you.'

“She heard me, and then she started to run away," Jameka told the outlet. When the suspect turned his attention towards him, she fought him off.

The Independent has contacted Philadelphia Police Department for comment. Anyone with information is asked to call the department on 215-686-TIPS (8477).

News.title: Boris Johnson’s Covid U-turns were like a ‘slow-moving car crash’, former aide says
News.content:

A series of Covid U-turns made by Boris Johnson’s government were like a “slow-moving car crash” that saw it make the same mistake “over and over again”, his former director of communications has said.

Lee Cain, who served in Downing Street from July 2019 until the end of 2020, told The Independent’s In the Room podcast that “avoidable” mistakes in No 10 would drive the communications team “bonkers”.

“It was just a slow-moving car crash, and that did happen quite particularly at the start of Covid,” he said. “It happened quite a few times. Luckily, I think, even in politics, once people make the same mistake over and over again, they did start listening.”

open image in gallery Lee Cain (right) was Boris Johnson’s director of communications ( AFP/Getty )

Mr Johnson was forced to make a number of significant U-turns during the pandemic, with several key policy decisions scrapped.

He repeatedly ruled out a second national lockdown both in and outside of the House of Commons - claiming in mid-October that Sir Keir Starmer’s support for a short term shutdown of the country was “the height of absurdity”. The second lockdown began on 5 November.

The then PM also famously encouraged all parents to send their children to school on the first day of term in January 2021, only to announce he was closing every school in England again that evening.

The previous August, amid intense and growing pressure, the government was forced into a humiliating U-turn when it announced it was dumping plans to base A-level results on a controversial algorithm, with ministers publicly apologising for the distress the fiasco had caused pupils and parents.

Mr Cain said there had been a discussion within No 10 at the start of the pandemic, about keeping pubs and bars open - but asking people not to visit them. That particular idea, he said, he thought had come from Mr Johnson himself.

open image in gallery The Covid pandemic erupted just months into Boris Johnson’s term as prime minister ( PA )

“I remember saying, as my sort of role as a sort of political Cassandra at the time, that perhaps this wasn't the best of all worlds… And I remember saying ‘This won't last 24 hours. We will not hold this position because people will simply ask, ‘If people shouldn't go, which you're suggesting, why don't we close the pubs and clubs?’”

He predicted that, had the plan gone ahead, “we would U-turn because that's what happened quite frequently at that point. So we'd U-turn very quickly. Boris would lament the whole thing and say, ‘Well, how did we get in this idea? I never thought of - I didn't want to do this. How did we end up in this position?’”

The situation was “bonkers because it was so avoidable,” he said, “...it was just a slow-moving car crash, and that did happen, particularly at the start of Covid it happened quite a few times. Luckily, I think... even in politics, once people make the same mistake over and over again, they did start listening.”

News.title: Top British scientist steps down from WHO
News.content:
One of Britain’s best-known scientists has resigned as assistant director-general of the World Health Organization.

Sir Jeremy Farrar became a household name during the pandemic when he served on the UK’s Scientific Advisory Group for Emergencies (Sage).

Sources inside the WHO and the broader scientific community told The Telegraph he resigned his position on Monday.

While it is not clear what prompted his resignation, colleagues told The Telegraph he had been unhappy within the organisation for some time. One speculated that he had become increasingly frustrated with its internal politics and bureaucracy.

Sir Jeremy, 64, who was also a former director of the Wellcome Trust, could not immediately be reached for comment.

The surprise move comes at a difficult time for the WHO, which is undergoing a major restructuring after suffering cuts and a massive funding shortfall following the United States’s withdrawal from it in January. It is also fighting a major outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the WHO’s Director-General, announced Dr Farrar’s decision in an email to all staff on Tuesday morning, saying that the British scientist will “retire” from the WHO, effective September 30.

In the email, seen by The Telegraph, Dr Tedros said: “Dr Farrar has demonstrated an exceptional commitment to science and public health at the highest levels, and we are grateful that he chose to bring his experience, energy and conviction to WHO.

“On behalf of the entire organisation, I extend my sincere thanks to Dr Farrar... [and wish] him every success in his next chapter and a well-deserved retirement.”

He added that Dr Bruce Aylward will take over as the new Assistant Director-General for Health Promotion, Disease Prevention and Care.

Another that perhaps warranted a higher price increase, the Brazilian only missed out on breaking the 200-point barrier due to his injury late in the season. News.title: Rabies deaths are rising. What is going wrong?
News.content:
In a packed intensive care ward in Dhaka, three-year-old Abdul lay paralysed, his tiny body contorted by a rabies infection that had reached his brain.

His mother, Sheuli Akter, 38, sat at his side massaging his legs in the hope that this might loosen his muscles, but it was having no effect. Even his hands and feet were seized up by cramps.

Abdul had been in the hospital for a month but doctors said he was unlikely to live much longer. The infection, they said, had progressed to degenerative encephalitis; the virus had got to his brain.

Abdul was shaking, gripped by fever. His breathing was rapid and panicked, punctuated occasionally by groans of pain.

On his chin was the telltale scar of a dog bite, the source of the infection.

“He was playing outside with the other children,” said Sheuli. “The dog, which was one of those always waiting around outside, suddenly attacked him. They said it went for him because he was the smallest.”

News.title: Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City
News.content:
Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the new signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

How about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

So what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

Title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

First Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

News.title: Rashford returns and Fernandes misses another penalty as Man Utd humbled by Amorim
News.content:
Manchester United 2 AC Milan 4

Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

News.title: Newcastle kit fiasco sums up haphazard pre-season
News.content:
Newcastle United 1 Bayer Leverkusen 2

Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.

The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.

During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.

Newcastle would go on to lose the game 2-1 in new manager Matthias Jaissle’s first game at St James’, a result which followed a 3-1 reverse against Everton on Wednesday evening.

Leverkusen, the 2023-24 Bundesliga champions now managed by Spaniard Carles Martínez Novell, scored after just 44 seconds through a powerful Ibrahim Maza strike.

News.title: Raul Jimenez’s late penalty seals share of spoils for Wolves against Blackburn
News.content:
Cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

Peixoto said: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

“We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

“We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”

Mowbray: It feels like a defeat

Tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

Mowbray said: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

“Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we showed there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”

The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

However, Wolves scored the first goal of the new campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

Sports.title: Mad transfer saga sees top flight fans occupy stadium and confront gun-toting owner over £27m sale of star player
Sports.content:
PAOK fans occupied their club’s stadium and demanded to speak to controversial owner Ivan Savvidis after star player Giannis Konstantelias was sold to Borussia Dortmund.

Konstantelias, 23, is one of the Greek club’s brightest academy products who went on to register a total of 44 goals and 26 assists in 190 appearances since joining the senior squad in 2021.



The playmaker led the Salonika outfit to the Super League title as well as the Greek Cup and helped his beloved team reach the quarter-finals of the Conference League two years ago.

However, PAOK agreed a near £22million deal with Dortmund, who signed the Greece international on a five-year contract that will see him bag £2.6m per year.



The agreement between the two sides includes an additional £5m in add-ons while Savvidis’ club also holds a resale value worth 17.5 per cent.

Konstantelias looks set to become PAOK’s most expensive sale – provided the above add-ons are triggered.



However, the fans were still left enraged as they staged a protest at their home ground of Toumba Stadium on Sunday.

SunSport understand about 400 supporters showed up, while some reportedly occupied PAOK’s offices inside the stadium.

The latter group also demanded explanations from Savvidis, 67, himself in a last-ditch attempt to convince him not to sell to Dortmund, who also have a close relationship with PAOK rivals Aris.

That came after the club’s most successful manager Razvan Lucescu also left this summer after winning two league titles and two Cups in seven years across two stints.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The PAOK owner made headlines eight years ago when he invaded the pitch at Toumba Stadium in a crunch clash against rivals AEK Athens after his team was controversially denied a late opener due to an offside call.

Savvidis barged in with a gun in his holster and was ultimately slapped with a three-year ban from Greek football stadiums as well as an £87,000 fine.

PAOK were docked three points and fined £55,000 due to their owner’s antics which also cost them the title in 2018.

Konstantelias was also approached by a fan upon his arrival at Dortmund airport and was put on a video call with the supporters gathered in Toumba to whom he reportedly explained it was his decision to leave.

The attacking midfielder came close to departing these past two years but PAOK managed to hold onto him.



Konstantelias was linked with a move to Red Bull Salzburg in 2024 but nothing came of it.

And Stuttgart came just a whisker away from landing him last year after a £15m deal, which included an extra £2m in add-ons and a 15 per cent resale clause.

Savvidis, though, pulled the plug at the eleventh hour after an intense reaction from the fans, with reports even suggesting he told him to return from Salonika airport just before he boarded a flight to Germany.

That led to a new contract until 2029 with significantly higher wages and a reported gentlemen’s agreement stating that the owner wouldn’t prevent the player leaving if he wished to.

Sports.title: Egypt boss Hossam Hassan ‘collapses due to extreme stress as his TWO wives brawl at bar’ then immediately divorces one
Sports.content:
EGYPT head coach Hossam Hassan collapsed due to extreme stress after his two wives got into a brawl, according to shock reports.

The 60-year-old was enjoying a break in Porto Marina when the pair came to blows.



An argument between his long-term wife Howaida Al-Gharbawi and second wife Dina “Dan Adam” Mustafa took place in a hotel bar, which then escalated into a physical fight in front of shocked onlookers.

Relatives quickly got involved, with security then called.



Both women were left with cuts and bruises.

Meanwhile, Al Arabiya reported that Hassan fainted due to stress after failing to stop the brawl.

But as per Sky News Arabia, his lawyer denied what he described as rumours that he had suffered a health crisis and stated that he was in good health.

In the aftermath, the Egypt manager is said to have divorced his first wife, Howaida.

He officially signed the divorce papers at a legal registrar’s office in Cairo.

Hassan had been with Howaida for decades prior to their sudden split.



Mohamed Shams, legal representative for second wife Dina, told Sky News Arabia: “We hoped it wouldn’t come to divorce, but things escalated to this level.”

Shams also stated that his client suffered a “premeditated attack” during the Porto Marina holiday.

Hassan has been head coach of Egypt since 2024 and led the nation to the World Cup last 16 this summer.

Egypt were knocked out of the tournament following a dramatic 3-2 defeat to Argentina in Atlanta.

The head coach later renewed his contract with the national team, keeping him in the position until 2030.

Sports.title: Champions League winner, 30, looks unrecognisable as he scores on debut for ninth-tier club
Sports.content:
A FORMER Champions League winner looked unrecognisable as he came out of retirement.

The star only announced his retirement from football in May.



That came off the back of a third major ACL injury.

However, still only 30, he is back in football – playing for a ninth-tier club.



The German was part of Bayern Munich‘s side that won the Champions League in 2020.

He also collected five Bundesliga medals, two DFB-Pokal Cups, the Super Cup and the Club World Cup for the Bavarians.

The defender – who played at two World Cups and earned 49 caps – added a Champions League runner-up medal in 2024, plus a silver medal at the 2016 Olympics for his country.

His final Bundesliga appearance came in May as a late sub for Borussia Dortmund in a 3-2 win over Eintracht Frankfurt.

But just three months later, the centre-back returned to the field in a familiar colour.

This time, though, he was sporting the yellow of his new team SV Tiefenbach, who play in the Kreisliga Baden-Wurttemberg – the ninth tier in Germany.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The bulky 6ft 5in giant even powered in a header to score on his debut.

However, he struggled to keep it tight at the back as Tiefenbach lost 7-2 to SG Kirchardt in their district league season opener.



The man wearing the No22 was none other than Niklas Sule.

Fans were delighted to see the famous face in action for Tiefenbach as he passed the ball around with ease, deployed in midfield rather than his traditional centre-back role, despite limited training time.

And he spent time after the match posing for selfies and signing autographs for supporters.

Coach Jason Walzel told Badische Neueste Nachrichten: “I think he’s enjoying it more playing a bit more offensively now.

“He was there on Saturday and then again on Thursday and Friday.



“I don’t think it was planned that he would one day actually play in the Kreisliga.

“The boys are happy, he’s a great guy.”

Sports.title: Ex-Man Utd legend Paul Scholes banned from road after clocking up two driving convictions in TWO days
Sports.content:
OWN GOAL Ex-Man Utd legend Paul Scholes banned from road after clocking up two driving convictions in TWO days

FORMER Man Utd legend Paul Scholes has been banned from the road after clocking up two driving offences in two days.

The midfielder, 51, was caught speeding at 37mph in a Range Rover in March while on a 30mph road in Cleckheaton in West Yorkshire.



Scholes was also rapped by Greater Manchester Police after a Mercedes registered in his name was clocked at 49mph in a 30mph zone in November last year.

The ex-England star was then prosecuted for failing to respond to two police letters asking for confirmation that he had been the speeding driver.



Both criminal cases wound up in court on two days last week – with Scholes handed a six-month driving ban.

The Class of 92 alumni was also ordered to pay fines, costs, and court fees totalling £1,472.



Scholes was prosecuted in private hearings under the Single Justice Procedure and convicted in his absence.

Court documents showed his Range Rover was caught speeding at just after 11.30pm on March 3.

Police said the former footballer replied to a notice of intended prosecution, confirming he had been the driver.

But Scholes could not be offered the chance of an out-of-court settlement with a speed awareness course as he is a “totter” – meaning he already had penalty points on his licence so faced a ban.



In the second case, Scholes’s Mercedes broke the speed limit on the A670 Mossley Road near Ashton-under-Lyne at 11.10am on November 14 last year.

Police said two letters were sent to his home and “no reply has been received”.

At court, the force dropped the speeding allegation but continued to prosecute Scholes for failing to reply to the letters.



On August 12 at Bradford Magistrates’ Court, he was handed a six-month driving ban for the speeding offence, along with a £220 fine, £120 costs, and an £88 victim surcharge.

The following day at Manchester Magistrates’ Court, Scholes was sentenced to a £660 fine, with six penalty points for his licence, £120 costs, and a £264 victim surcharge.

Scholes won 11 Premier League titles, three FA Cups and the Champions League twice in a glittering career at Man United.

The former midfielder was also capped 66 times by England.

Sports.title: Rio Ferdinand’s wife Kate labelled ‘Ibiza Queen’ as she parties in see-through outfit on wild night with Man Utd icon
Sports.content:
RIO FERDINAND showed off his dance moves at a nightclub in Ibiza ahead of the new Premier League season – and his wife Kate caught the eye with her choice of outfit.

The Manchester United icon, 47, has been enjoying some free time after working for Fox Sports at the World Cup.



Ferdinand and his wife Kate, who tied the knot in 2019, let their hair down after jetting out to Ibiza.

The loved-up couple were spotted partying on a wild night out ahead of the former England defender’s return to broadcasting duties for the upcoming campaign.





Kate, 35, gave fans a glimpse of their memorable trip to Ibiza by uploading nightclub snaps onto Instagram.

The TV personality, who is negotiating a mega-money deal to appear on I’m A Celebrity: Wild Frontier with Ferdinand, showed off her stunning figure by donning a brown crop top and a pair of see-through trousers.

And Kate left her 1.4million Instagram followers rushing into the comments section.

One said: “The Ibiza Queen has risen.”



Another added: “Absolutely gorgeous.”

A third Kate fan chimed in: “You look amazing.”



A fourth noted: “Looking insane.”

And a fifth simply claimed: “Unbelievable.”

The photos were uploaded onto social media just days after Kate hit back at claims she is with Ferdinand for the cash.

Speaking on her Blended podcast, she said: “People think I’m a gold digger, I’m with him for money. I’m basically his nanny that he doesn’t pay.



“I always say if I wanted to pick a rich man I could have picked a lot easier one without all the kids.

“I’m here because I love you, there are great things and there are hard things.”

Sports.title: Inside Pep’s 35-year marriage with ‘most beautiful woman on the planet’ & how ‘losing the passion’ lead to secret split
Sports.content:
PEP TALK Inside Pep’s 35-year marriage with ‘most beautiful woman on the planet’ & how ‘losing the passion’ lead to secret split

HE was with her from the age of 18 and has described her as the “most beautiful woman on the planet”, but Pep Guardiola’s marriage was crumbling behind the scenes long before he announced his split.

The Man City boss, 55, who’s been with the club since 2016, is expected to speak about his marriage breakdown on A Beautiful Obsession, a four-part series dropping on Amazon Prime tomorrow.



In a sweary rant shown in the preview, following a 2-0 Champions League loss to Juventus, he told his team: “Guys – I want to confess something.

“I’m f***ing divorced from the most beautiful woman on your planet. It’s my wife – my ex-wife. I love her unbelievably. But we lost the passion.



“For many reasons, we lost the passion. I love her absolutely. She loves me, yeah, but we lost the passion. And it’s how you play football. You play because of something inside — but where is the passion?”

Pep split from Cristina Serra, 54, in December 2024. They had been married 10 years, but their romance spanned more than three decades.

They are parents to Maria and Marius, who are in their 20s, and Valentina, who is a teenager.

Their relationship began when an 18-year-old Pep went to a fashion store in Barcelona owned by Cristina’s family, to model some outfits by Spanish designer Antonio Miro.



Back then, Pep was playing for Barcelona’s B team, while she was an actress who had appeared on Spanish TV.

Pep’s sister Francesca once recalled: “He was very handsome, a good student, always getting good marks. The teachers drooled over him, he was already seductive when he was little.”

Cristina gave up acting to concentrate on her clothing business and is now said to be worth more than £30million.

Meanwhile, Pep established himself as one of the best midfielders of his generation, winning multiple titles with Barcelona’s first team, before launching one of the most successful managerial careers of all time.

Pep always credited his wife with his great sense of fashion and for bringing up his children. She moved with him to Manchester when he joined City, with the couple taking up residence in a luxury block in Salford.



Cristina was so important to the Spaniard that he even refused to join any team without her say-so. In a rare personal interview in 2018, he said: “Only at home I feel safe.

“I mean safe in terms of not being observed. I close the door and I feel safe. My job is demanding a lot. Cristina is an incredible woman, not just an incredible mother.

“If we were talking about moving to New York, Munich and here, if she decides not to come, I won’t come.



“I will not be here, I cannot be alone in this kind of job without my family.”

But cracks started to show in 2019, when Cristina returned to Barcelona with their youngest child Valentina, while Pep stayed in Manchester.

She had been unable to settle in the North West and yearned to be close to the Catalan capital.

While they put on a united front on holidays and at Wimbledon, in private, their recent long-distance relationship was becoming increasingly unsustainable.

Their split was announced in January 2025 however Spanish property documents — obtained by The Sun — showed the couple were dividing their assets much earlier.



Pep became the sole owner of their £8.5million family home, in the Barcelona suburb of Pedralbes, on October 7, 2024.

A source told The Sun last year: “Pep and Cristina had long been living separate lives.

“She was unable to settle in Manchester and returned to Spain but they appeared, on the surface at least, to make it work.

“When they announced they were separating in January, his decision to sign a new contract at Manchester City was conveniently blamed.

“It may well have been the final straw, but they appear to have decided to end it much earlier than anyone knew or realised.



“They were already starting to part ways before he put pen to paper on his new deal.”

Another source said: “They were dividing assets long before all but their closest circle had a hint anything was amiss.

“It tells you a lot about when minds were made up.”



Meanwhile, Cristina made a fresh start of her own, buying a luxury rooftop duplex near one of Barcelona’s most famous streets, La Rambla.

Cristina purchased the sprawling three-bedroom, five-bathroom pad in September 2025, with well-placed sources saying she paid just under £3million for it.

The apartment is a mere two minutes from the family-owned Serra Claret designer fashion store she runs.

A source said at the time: “All the talk has been about Pep buying himself a bachelor pad.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“But the fact Cristina has bought her own place in the city centre and he has become the sole owner of the old family home points to her being the one that will do the moving.”



Another insider added: “The likely scenario for the future will involve Cristina moving nearer her place of work and Pep using the villa as his main base when he’s back in town unless he decides to rent it out and opt for somewhere smaller.”

Sports.title: World Cup stadium could be demolished as consultation is launched on future of 35,950-seater ground
Sports.content:
HELLAS VERONA’S stadium, the Stadio Marcantonio Bentegodi, is set to be demolished and rebuilt smaller – but more modern – in time for Euro 2032.

Italy hosts the 19th iteration of the Euros along with Turkey and this stadium was actually used when they hosted the World Cup in 1990.



Back then, an extra tier of seating and a roof was added to the ground, but now, the stadium must be updated.

Damiano Tommasi, a former Italy international and Roma legend – who also started his career at Verona – is now the mayor of the city and is tasked with developing the project.



The former midfielder wants to keep the same location and that means finding a group to finance the rebuild. Tommasi has two private options on the table that will cover the £171 million cost.

Tommasi keeps insisting: “We are moving forward with the upgrade process for the Bentegodi Stadium with the goal of making it compliant with the European Football Championship 2032.”

This would involve demolishing the current building and rebuilding it smaller, but with world-leading technologies like a retractable pitch to accommodate concerts and turn the stadium into a multipurpose facility.

But the works would also help the regeneration of the area and neighborhoods, creating more space for greenery and gardens, and improving road layouts.

Tommasi said: “With respect to our intention to proceed with the expression of interest, a new phase has begun, and so we can now open the proposal to anyone interested.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK



“Obviously, there are other requirements regarding the detailed presentation of the project.”

One group said to be interested is ASM Global, a company with offices in the US, Europe, and Italy (Milan), which has already created the new Chorus Life in Bergamo, a state-of-the-art, multipurpose stadium.

They also oversaw the redevelopment of the Real Madrid‘s Santiago Bernabeu and Barcelona‘s Camp Nou.

Sports.title: Loved-up Alex Scott and Jess Glynne strip down to bikinis as couple enjoy romantic Greek getaway
Sports.content:
LIONESSES legend Alex Scott and partner Jess Glynne treated fans to a glimpse of their romantic holiday in a stunning social media post.

The former Arsenal right-back, 41, was part of the BBC’s broadcasting team at the World Cup.



And Scott decided to soak up the sun after seeing Spain win the summer extravaganza.

She has been enjoying a romantic Greek getaway with partner Glynne ahead of the new Premier League season.





The loved-up couple, who started dating in 2023, stripped down to their bikinis in snaps shared on Instagram.

Scott also drove a boat and sipped some wine as she switched off from presenting duties.

And the ex-defender, who has more free time after Football Focus was canned at the end of last season, hit the gym to maintain her physique.

Fans raced into the comments section to rave over Scott and hitmaker Glynne, 36.



One said: “Power couple.”

Another added: “Love seeing your holiday pics. Keep smiling.”



A third chimed in: “You look so happy, lovely couple.”

A fourth noted: “Love this, love you two together.”

And a fifth simply claimed: “Gorgeous.”

Scott bagged a whopping 140 caps for the Lionesses and was part of the squad which came third in the 2015 Women’s World Cup.



She also enjoyed trophy-laden spells with Arsenal, either side of a stint in the USA with Boston Breakers.

But Scott then hung up her boots in 2018 and moved into broadcasting with the BBC.

Sports.title: What next for LIV Golf? Timeline from big beginnings to uncertain future
Sports.content:
The LIV Golf League is ending the 2026 season with its long-term future unclear, having been a dominant discussion point during a turbulent few years for men’s professional golf.

Its arrival earlier in the decade sparked division and debate in a fractured men's game, with players leaving the PGA Tour and DP World Tour to join the breakaway circuit.

A shock framework agreement between the PGA Tour, DP World Tour and Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) was unable to unify men's golf, with LIV Golf facing fresh challenges to retain its place in the sport.

From its initial inception and increasing growth through to players leaving and cuts in funding, we look at the timeline of LIV Golf's history so far...

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rory McIlroy reflected on the running of the PGA Tour before LIV came along and shared his concerns over future schedules

October 2021: LIV Golf Investments was officially announced and two-time Open champion Greg Norman revealed as the league's founding CEO.

February 2022: In an interview with Golf Digest, Phil Mickelson criticised the PGA Tour's policy on player media rights. He said: "It was the tour's obnoxious greed that has really opened the door for opportunities elsewhere." He later told journalist Alan Shipnuck that the Saudis were "scary m************ to be involved with".

March 2022: LIV Golf announced it would launch an eight-tournament schedule on June 9, titled the LIV Invitational Series. The total prize pot for the eight events was set at £191.32m ($255m).

May 2022: Norman branded the PGA Tour "anti-competitive", after the US circuit denied players their release requests to play in LIV Golf events. Former Masters champions Dustin Johnson and Sergio Garcia were revealed among the first group of players to tee up at LIV's inaugural event in London.

June 2022: Mickelson confirmed he would play in LIV Golf's first event, won by Charl Schwartzel. The PGA Tour sent a letter to its members announcing those in the field at LIV Golf London were suspended indefinitely. Bryson DeChambeau and Brooks Koepka both joined the breakaway league ahead of its second event.

July 2022: The DP World Tour issued fines of £100,000 ($133,921) to LIV players who featured in LIV Golf London. Meanwhile, LIV Golf submitted an application for its players to be given Official World Golf Ranking (OWGR) points.

July 2022: Henrik Stenson sent shockwaves through the golfing world by joining LIV Golf and was subsequently stripped of his role as Team Europe's captain for the 2023 Ryder Cup in Italy.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Padraig Harrington said in 2022 he was disappointed that Henrik Stenson did not wait until after the 2023 Ryder Cup to join LIV Golf

August 2022: A group of 11 LIV Golf players, including Mickelson, Ian Poulter and Johnson, filed an antitrust lawsuit against the PGA Tour. LIV Golf later joined the lawsuit. After winning The Open at St Andrews and at the end of the PGA Tour season, Cameron Smith became the latest player to join LIV Golf.

September 2022: Rory McIlroy likened LIV Golf to a "soap opera" and said his relationship with some of his Ryder Cup team-mates who joined LIV had been damaged.

October 2022: The PGA Tour filed a federal lawsuit against Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) and Yasir Al-Rumayyan, the governor of the PIF.

November 2022: McIlroy called for Norman to leave the rebel league and Tiger Woods also encouraged Norman to go in order for a peace settlement to be negotiated.

December 2022: Augusta National chairman Fred Ridley confirmed eligible LIV Golfers could play at The Masters. Jon Rahm said PGA Tour players should be 'thankful' for LIV.

January 2023: Patrick Reed and McIlroy were involved in the 'tee-gate' saga, where Reed flicked a 4Aces GC tee at the Northern Irishman after the American accused McIlroy of ignoring him.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McIlroy played down talk of a confrontation with Patrick Reed but added he was not interested in talking to him on the course

February 2023: The DP World Tour and LIV Golf went to court for an arbitration hearing, held over five days.

April 2023: The DP World Tour won its legal battle against players who elected to join LIV Golf, enabling them to impose £100,000 ($134,706) fines against LIV players for competing in conflicting events.

May 2023: Koepka became the first LIV Golfer to win a major at the PGA Championship, lifting the Wanamaker Trophy for a third time.

June 2023: The PGA Tour, DP World Tour and PIF announce a shock 'framework agreement', where the organisations ended all pending lawsuits and said they wanted to cooperate to "unify the game of golf".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The deal between the PGA Tour, DP World Tour and Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund dominated the news agenda at the 2023 US Open

McIlroy hit back at the announcement, saying he felt like a "sacrificial lamb", while PGA Tour commissioner Jay Monahan faced calls to resign.

October 2023: LIV Golf lost its initial bid to be awarded OWGR points.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dustin Johnson said in 2022 that LIV players should earn official world ranking points but did not expect retrospective points from events earlier in the series

December 2023: Rahm, who won The Masters in April, joined LIV Golf for a deal reportedly worth up to £450m ($607.7m).

January 2024: Tyrrell Hatton follows Rahm to LIV Golf for a then-reported fee of £47.3m ($60m).

February 2024: Anthony Kim ended a 12-year absence from professional golf by joining the breakaway league. McIlroy softened his stance on LIV Golf, saying players who joined the rebel league should be allowed to come back to the PGA Tour.

March 2024: Norman confirmed LIV Golf had withdrawn its application for OWGR points. Woods formed part of a delegation of PGA Tour members to meet with LIV Golf powerbrokers, including Al-Rumayyan, in the Bahamas, to discuss the merger. PGA Tour commissioner Monahan said the talks were "constructive".

April 2024: McIlroy denied claims he was previously close to joining LIV Golf.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McIlroy reassured fans immediately after the framework agreement was announced that he still 'hated LIV Golf'

June 2024: DeChambeau claimed a one-shot victory at the US Open, following Koepka as the second LIV player to win a major, after McIlroy's dramatic late collapse at Pinehurst No 2.

September 2024: The PGA of America confirmed LIV Golfers would be eligible to play for Team USA at the Ryder Cup the following year.

October 2024: Monahan and Al-Rumayyan played together at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship, signalling that merger talks were progressing.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player PGA Tour commissioner Jay Monahan and LIV Golf's Yasir Al-Rumayyan were paired at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship

January 2025: Norman was replaced as LIV Golf's CEO by Scot O'Neil. McIlroy praised Norman for "getting LIV Golf off the ground".

February 2025: Woods joined Al-Rumayyan and Adam Scott for talks at the White House with US President Donald Trump regarding the ongoing merger.

March 2025: Monahan said Trump's involvement in ongoing talks between golf's key stakeholders made the prospect of a reunification between the tours "very real".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McIlroy said in 2025 that the introduction of LIV Golf had benefited the players financially

November 2025: Having launched a fresh bid for OWGR points in July, LIV looked to enhance its push by expanding from 54-hole events to a 72-hole format, a move which McIlroy called "peculiar".

December 2025: Koepka announced he was leaving LIV Golf due to personal reasons. He then confirmed his return to the PGA Tour via the Returning Member Program, where he was subjected to certain conditions and required to make a £3.7m ($5m) donation to charity.

January 2026: Reed also confirmed his departure from LIV Golf and returned to play on the DP World Tour.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brandel Chamblee explained why he felt LIV had made golf less competitive in the majors

February 2026: LIV Golf was granted world ranking points by the OWGR, but the breakaway league's bosses criticised the allocation of ranking points LIV players could receive - only the top 10 and ties - as "unfair".

The DP World Tour offered conditional releases to eight members, including Hatton, provided they paid off their outstanding fines. Rahm insisted he had "no intention" of paying his fines.

March 2026: Rahm withdrew his appeal against sanctions imposed by the DP World Tour for playing in conflicting LIV Golf events. His fines were believed to be around £2.2m ($3m). He said the tour's conditional release programme was "extorting players".

April 2026: The PIF confirmed it was pulling its funding of LIV at the end of 2026 but it was funded through the rest of the season. LIV released a statement saying it was looking for external investors to finance the series going forward. PGA Tour commissioner Brian Rolapp said the tour was thinking about pathways to reinstate LIV players.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bryson DeChambeau claimed that LIV Golf players were left 'surprised' by the Saudi Public Investment Fund's decision to withdraw funding

May 2026: Rahm agreed to pay his outstanding DP World Tour penalties and ensure he remained eligible to play at the 2027 Ryder Cup. Elsewhere, US President Trump backed LIV Players to return to the PGA Tour.

DeChambeau said his future on the PGA Tour depended on whether players wanted him back, as speculation mounted over whether he would agree a new LIV Golf contract.

July 2026: Rahm said he was hopeful LIV Golf could continue but was tight-lipped on what the future would hold for the league.

August 2026: After much speculation, LIV Golf CEO O'Neil said the league had found a new lead investor, although was unable to provide details. The league also said players would become majority equity holders.

August 2026: LIV Golf finally confirmed its season-ending Team Championship in Michigan would no longer go ahead, following weeks of speculation, seeing the 2026 campaign finish a week early in Indianapolis.

Sports.title: US Amateur champion Whaley and Poulter's son named in GB&I Walker Cup team
Sports.content:
US Amateur champion Jack Whaley has been selected in the Great Britain and Ireland team for the 2026 Walker Cup against the USA.

The 22-year-old Englishman forms part of a 10-strong squad, alongside Ian Poulter's son Luke - one of six returning players from the 2025 staging of the event at Cypress Point in California.

Great Britain and Ireland will be looking to beat the USA for the first time since 2015 - and their 16½-9½ triumph at Royal Lytham & St Annes - when the 51st Walker Cup takes place at Lahinch Golf Club in County Clare, Ireland - live on Sky Sports from September 5-6.

Amateur Champion Stuart Grehan and Connor Graham, who will make his third successive appearance, return along with Eliot Baker, Poulter, Niall Sheils Donegan and Tyler Weaver.

The full GB&I team Eliot Baker, England, Tiverton, 23

Ben Bolton, England, Enville, 19

Sam Easterbrook, England, Olton, 21

Connor Graham, Scotland, Blairgowrie, 19

Stuart Grehan, Ireland, County Louth, 33

Josh Hill, England, Fox Den, 22

Luke Poulter, England, Woburn, 22

Niall Sheils Donegan, Scotland, Meadow Club, 21

Tyler Weaver, England, Bury St Edmunds, 21

Jack Whaley, England, Rotherham, 22

(Reserve) Thomas Higgins, Ireland, Roscommon, 23

(Reserve) David Howard, Ireland, Fota Island, 27

Ben Bolton, Sam Easterbrook, Josh Hill and Whaley will make their Walker Cup debuts. Irish pair Thomas Higgins and David Howard have been named as first and second reserve, respectively.

Also returning for another crack at beating the USA is GB&I captain Dean Robertson, who admitted that Whaley would not have been one of his picks to make the team had he not won the US Amateur.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jack Whaley sensationally chipped in on his way to winning the US Amateur title

The Doncaster-born golfer defeated American Jay Leng Jr in a gruelling 36-hole final on Sunday to become just the third English player in history to win the tournament following on from Harold Hilton in 1911 and current world No 4 Matt Fitzpatrick in 2013.

"Before last week, I wouldn't have seen Jack in the team," Robertson admitted. "But after watching him, the talent he's got and the humility that he's got - the way that he spoke - I'm really excited to welcome him.

"The only downside of that is that if it wasn't for Jack, Tom Higgins would have been in the team, 100 per cent."

What is the Walker Cup? The Walker Cup Match is a biennial 10-man amateur team competition between a team composed of players from Great Britain and Ireland and the USA. It is played over two days with 18 singles matches and eight foursomes matches. The USA leads the overall series 40-9-1.

Robertson added: "We have a really exciting blend of players who have experienced the Walker Cup before and others who have earned their first opportunity through some excellent performances over the last year.

"We have players who have won important championships, performed at the highest level in amateur golf and demonstrated that they can deliver results in international match play.

"We know there will be fantastic support for the team in Ireland and our players will be determined to give those supporters plenty to get behind.

"We learned a great deal from Cypress Point and everyone involved is hugely motivated by the challenge ahead."

Sports.title: The Premier League is back! All 20 clubs assessed
Sports.content:
Football hasn't stopped this summer, so to make sure you're up to speed with how every Premier League is shaping up ahead of the new season we've taken a look at their preparations for the new campaign.

From new managers and new signings to pre-season form and emerging talents, here's the lowdown on how the top 20 are looking...

Image: Christos Tzolis impressed at the Emirates on his home debut against Dortmund last week

A lot of Arsenal's transfer talk has surrounded Vinicius Junior and Bradley Barcola this summer, but has Christos Tzolis given Mikel Arteta a reason to think differently?

There was not a great deal of fanfare when the Greek winger moved for £34m from Club Brugge early in the window, but Tzolis has shown quite a lot of threat since arriving.

In six pre-season games, Tzolis has six assists and one goal - including making two in the Community Shield against Man City. He is by no means flashy - he completed none of his dribbles in the win in Cardiff, for example - but he is very effective.

That pre-season form mirrored his form last season - getting 51 goal contributions in 52 games for Club Brugge. A set-piece threat too; if he gets anything close to those numbers in the regular season, then Arsenal have found themselves a £34m bargain.

Sam Blitz

Arsenal

Coventry City Friday 21st August 6:30pm Kick off 8:00pm

Image: Brian Madjo announced himself to Aston Villa with a goal against PSG in the Super Cup

The doom and gloom mood of pre-season following the departures of Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans was momentarily lifted with the performance of Aston Villa against Paris Saint-Germain in the UEFA Super Cup final.

New signing Joao Gomes and 17-year-old Brian Madjo have impressed in pre-season and stood out once again against PSG, despite the loss.

However, Unai Emery was dealt another blow when reports emerged of injuries for both players as they approach the season opener against Brighton. They will now join both Amadou Onana and new signing Johan Manzambi on the sidelines.

It has been a summer of change at Villa Park and navigating key player exits is difficult enough. Injuries and the absence of any form of pre-season for Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins due to their extended World Cup breaks now mean both the line-up and performance itself could throw up a few surprises at the Amex Stadium.

Pat Rowe

Image: Former Leipzig coach Marco Rose has taken the reins at Bournemouth this summer

After a free-scoring pre-season under new head coach Marco Rose there are hopes that life after Andoni Iraola can be just as bright for Bournemouth despite a first season in Europe to contend with.

The Cherries' succession plan is as strong for players as it is for managers and Rose will tinker with rather than overhaul Iraola's work and getting their transfer business done early has helped his squad settle ahead of their most testing season.

An injury to Eli Kroupi Junior's foot injury will stop him from carrying on his superb form from last season for the foreseeable but there is already intrigue about the prospect of Alvaro Rodriguez, a summer arrival from Elche.

There are concerns over a lack of depth in central defence, especially with 22-year-old Antonio Silva expected to slot straight in to replace Marcos Senesi. But the ex-Benfica man has plenty of pedigree, making 20 appearances for Portugal already and 41 in the Champions League.

Ron Walker

Goal difference alone prevented the Bees from qualifying for Europe in May, but that's been forgotten now.

They've spent over £60m this summer, breaking their transfer record to sign Mali international midfielder Mamadou Sangare from Lens, while also adding proven Premier League players Callum Wilson and Jaidon Anthony to bolster the attack.

Dan Long

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fabian Hurzeler told Sky Sports how Brighton can move forward after losing Danny Welbeck to Chelsea

It was a blow to Brighton to lose Danny Welbeck in the summer - but few fans will begrudge him the move at this stage of his career after he gave a lot to the club. Likewise, Brighton will feel they got brilliant money in for Jan Paul van Hecke and Carl Rushworth - the latter of which could be challenging James Trafford for the England jersey in the coming years.

In terms of incomings, it's the usual case of 'trust the process' with Brighton's recruitment team. The incredible hit rate has slowed a little in recent times, but the club have generally rebuilt pretty well year on year.

Simeon Gholam

Brighton and Hove Albion

Aston Villa Sunday 23rd August 1:00pm Kick off 2:00pm

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' David Richardson's discusses whether Chelsea will replicate Bayer Leverkusen's tactics under new boss Xabi Alonso

Xabi Alonso appears to be replicating his successful 3-4-3 formation, which delivered the Bundesliga title for Bayer Leverkusen, at Chelsea after testing the system in pre-season.

Alonso had fielded a 4-2-3-1 in their first three friendlies, but after switching to a back three against AC Milan - their best performance of the summer in a 3-0 win - it seems he could stick with it heading into their opening match against Fulham on Monday Night Football.

Maxence Lacroix was at the heart of the back three in their final pre-season game against Real Sociedad while Morgan Rogers started on the left of a dangerous frontline including Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer. Marco Palestra struggled at left-wing back with Pedro Neto operating on the other side. It remains a work in progress.

That belief could be tested with an extremely difficult opener at Arsenal on Friday night but after 25 years away expect Coventry and their fans to relish their Premier League return.

Peter Smith

Crystal Palace started pre-season with a new manager in Pierre Sage, but the Frenchman's attempts to implement a new playing style have been hampered as a host of first-team players were focused on the World Cup, rather than an opening 5-1 win over Swindon Town.

The reappearance of Matheus Franca, a forgotten Brazilian youngster, has been one of the rare positives as he scored a hat-trick against Swindon and has featured regularly.
